candidates.tagline: 30 signs. 45 trucks. Zero fixes. Louisville's Can Opener is still hungry.
candidates.story: During Louisville's I-65 closure (June–August 2026), GPS rerouted 125,000 daily vehicles past a railroad underpass with 11-foot-8 clearance — peeling the roofs off 45 tractor-trailers in two months while officials' only response was adding more warning signs (now 30+).
candidates.why_funny: The official solution to a bridge that destroys roughly one truck per day is to keep stapling more signs to things, earning the bridge its own community memorial website, t-shirt line, and the nickname 'Can Opener' — while the fix (raise or lower the road) sits in the 'too expensive' pile.
candidates.alt: Black-and-white photo of a box truck crammed under Louisville's Third Street railroad overpass, its roof buckled against the bridge with the LOW CLEARANCE 11-8 ALL TRUCKS sign hanging directly above the point of impact, debris on the road

candidates.tagline: Built a metro viaduct next to an airport. Forgot to check if planes could fly over it.
candidates.story: Mumbai's Metro Line 7A viaduct near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport was fully constructed before anyone noticed the overhead electrification poles exceed the airport funnel zone by 2.5 metres — potentially requiring demolition of nearly 1 km of brand-new elevated track worth ₹250 crore ($30M).
candidates.why_funny: Engineers designed, approved, and built a metro viaduct beside one of India's busiest airports and somehow failed to check airport height clearance rules at any stage of the design or construction — the consultant is blamed for not 'highlighting and factoring in' aviation restrictions that are publicly available.
candidates.alt: Editorial composite showing blue-and-red Mumbai Metro 7A trains on elevated track alongside Mumbai Airport's iconic canopy interior, with overlay text reading 'Metro 7A Viaduct At Risk — MMRDA Says Consultant Missed OHE Height'
